# zen-proxy

> A local, zero-dependency proxy that lets **any** coding agent use opencode's anonymous **free** Zen models — no accounts, no API keys. It speaks **two wire formats**: the OpenAI API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/models`) for Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Aider, mimo CLI and opencode forks, and the **Anthropic Messages API** (`/v1/messages`) so **Claude Code works as-is**, tools included. For Claude Code it is a single command: `zen-claude`.

## The problem this solves

opencode's Zen gateway serves its free models (`big-pickle`, `space-bunny-free`, `nemotron-*-free`, `deepseek-*-free`, etc. — the exact set changes; `GET /v1/models` is authoritative) **only to requests that mimic the opencode client**.

- With the right UA plus the `x-opencode-session` **and** `x-opencode-session-id` headers, `POST https://opencode.ai/inference/v1/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer public` returns HTTP 200.
- Without a session header the gateway returns **400 MissingSessionID**; with only one of the two session headers it returns **403 FreeTierError**.
- The legacy `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` base still answers `/models` but rejects genuine agent traffic with **403 FreeTierError**. The served base is `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1`.
- Most agents force their own UA and never send a session header, so they cannot use the free tier directly.

zen-proxy solves this by injecting the correct `User-Agent` and a stable per-client `x-opencode-session` pair upstream, then re-exposing everything on `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1` — as either a standard OpenAI API or a standard Anthropic Messages API.

## Key facts

- **Endpoints**: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (stream + non-stream), `POST /v1/responses`, `GET /v1/models`, `GET /health`, dashboard at `GET /`.
- **Auth**: anonymous via `Bearer public`; BYOK via `defaultZenKey` config or an `x-zen-key` / real bearer token.
- **Session**: opencode's free tier requires `x-opencode-session`. The proxy mints one per client (stable per source IP, or one shared id for local clients) when the caller doesn't send one; set `injectSession: false` to disable.
- **Quota**: the free tier is per-IP; the proxy forwards the real client IP (`x-real-ip`/`x-forwarded-for` when `trustForwarded` is on), but for local/loopback clients it omits `x-real-ip` so upstream counts your machine's real IP — matching opencode direct usage and avoiding a bogus shared `127.0.0.1` bucket. Do not abuse or rotate IPs.
- **Anthropic API**: `POST /v1/messages` (+ `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) are translated to the target model's endpoint family and back, streaming included, so Claude Code can point at it via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` (the `zen-claude` command sets this for you). Because the free tier only accepts requests carrying opencode's own tools, the proxy attaches opencode's built-in tools alongside the caller's (only ones the caller has a counterpart for) and renames calls back — the caller's system prompt is never modified.
- **Model fallback**: reads the free-model list from `models.json`, which a GitHub Action keeps current from opencode's public catalog every 6 hours. Tries them in order on 429/5xx **and** on model-level 4xx (`Model is unavailable`, `FreeTierError`, geo-blocked or unsupported models), honors `retry-after`.
- **Claude Code, one command**: run `zen-claude`. There is no separate step — it starts the proxy if it is not already running, waits for it to answer, registers every live free Zen model in Claude Code's `/model` picker, launches Claude Code, and stops the proxy again when you exit. The installer puts `zen-claude` on your PATH (Linux/macOS and Windows alike, alongside `zen-proxy`; `claude-zen` is linked too as an alias). If Claude Code is not installed it says so, prints `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, and exits without starting a proxy. It passes `claude --settings <file>` rather than exported env, because Claude Code reads env from `~/.claude/settings.json` and that wins over your shell; your existing Claude Code config is never modified.
- **Endpoint routing**: Zen serves each model on either `/v1/chat/completions` or `/v1/responses`. `responsesModels` lists the patterns (`*` allowed); the proxy translates requests, tool calls, reasoning and SSE streams in both directions, so any OpenAI-compatible client works either way.
- **Free-tier gate**: opencode serves free models only to genuine agent traffic. A request needs a valid session pair (`x-opencode-session` + `x-opencode-session-id`), `stream: true`, and a system message carrying opencode's own wording; anything else gets `403 FreeTierError: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`. The request must also carry a tool named `read`: measured against the live gateway every other name in the manifest (`bash`, `edit`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`) is refused. Requests that carry no tools at all — an agent's internal call, like summarization or title generation — therefore get opencode's whole manifest attached, which is what opencode itself sends on every call; `/v1/chat/completions` also asks for `tool_choice: "none"` (the Responses API takes only `"auto"`), but the gateway ignores it and answers a plain summarization prompt with real tool calls, so tool calls are stripped from the reply on both routes. A request that brings its own tools and pins one of them with `tool_choice` — a forced-tool helper, like a title or label call — needs the same `read` in the list or the gateway refuses the whole request, so the proxy adds a **stub** named `read` for exactly those calls: the gate looks at the tool's name and nothing else, and the pin is what makes adding one safe. Your tool list and your pin are forwarded untouched. The pin is not enforcement — the provider may still answer with a call you never offered — so the injected tool is deliberately a stub the model has no reason to pick. `user-agent` is irrelevant. That is not the model being broken: such models are shown as `agent-only`, never pruned, and the proxy learns their true health from real client traffic (`ok (live traffic)`). Agents that stream (Claude Code, Cline, Roo, Continue, Aider, mimo, opencode) work as-is; one-shot non-streaming calls fall back transparently and the reply carries `zen_served_by` / `x-zen-served-by`. No synthetic probe can verify a free model — a retired one is refused identically — so the proxy learns true health from real client traffic (`ok (live traffic)`). Which free models exist comes from opencode's public `/models` catalog, kept current in `models.json` by the model-sync Action every 6 hours; the proxy reads that file at startup and follows it unless your config pins its own list.
- **Rate limiting**: optional per-client limit on chat requests (`rateLimitMax`, `0` = off). `/health` and the dashboard are never throttled.
- **Model aliases**: `modelAliases` maps any name (e.g. `gpt-4o`) to a free model; reply model is rewritten back.
- **Config**: `zen-proxy.json` (hot-reloaded) or env vars: `PORT`, `HOST`, `ZEN_URL`, `ZEN_UA`, `INJECT_SESSION`, `AUTO_UA`, `UA_REFRESH_MS`, `PROBE_AUTH`, `RESPONSES_MODELS`, `RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `DEFAULT_MODEL`, `FALLBACK_MODELS`, `MODEL_ALIASES`, `PROXY_KEY`, `ZEN_KEY`, `TRUST_FORWARDED`, `TIMEOUT_MS`, `CACHE_MS`, `AUTO_SYNC`, `AUTO_SYNC_MS`, `ZEN_PROXY_CONFIG`.
- **Auto model sync**: probes every upstream free model with a tiny completion (sending a session header, matching real traffic) and updates the config automatically. Only definitively-gone models (`not supported`, 404) are removed — temporary blocks (`403 FreeTierError`, geo, timeouts) keep the model configured so it recovers by itself. `probeAuth` picks the probe credentials (`auto` / `anonymous` / `key`). A GitHub Action keeps the shipped list in the repo current too.
- **Requirements**: Node.js >= 18. Zero npm dependencies.

## Install

```bash
# Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.sh | bash

# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Or clone and run: `git clone https://github.com/12errh/zen-proxy.git && cd zen-proxy && node zen-proxy.mjs`

## Point any agent at it

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "zen": {
      "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1",
      "apiKey": "public",
      "models": { "space-bunny-free": {} }
    }
  }
}
```

Quick test:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"space-bunny-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'
```
